```json
{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Each XD module will be ported as a Spring Cloud Stream 'processor' module using the s-c-s MessageChannel-based API (transform/filter pattern) rather than XD's custom Module/Channel abstractions.",
    "The script module will support both Groovy and shell-like scripting by leveraging Spring's ScriptFactory abstractions, with a unified processor contract.",
    "The shell module will execute external processes via Java's ProcessBuilder, with a Spring Boot @ConfigurationProperties class exposing command/argument options.",
    "The splitter module will be implemented as a Spring Integration splitter wrapped as a s-c-s processor, supporting SpEL or lambda expressions.",
    "The json-to-tuple module will reuse the existing Tuple data structure from Spring Cloud Stream core, mapping JSON objects to Tuple fields.",
    "The object-to-json module will use Jackson's ObjectMapper with configurable type information, exposed as a s-c-s @Transformer bean.",
    "The BinderFactory abstraction will be modeled as a Spring FactoryBean< Binder > keyed by binder type (e.g., 'kafka', 'rabbit'), with a default implementation backed by Spring Boot auto-configuration.",
    "The composed job removal exploration (U6) will be delivered as an analysis spike only (no code removal in this increment), producing a written design document with options and trade-offs.",
    "The ZK metadata job definition exploration (U7) will be delivered as a design spike producing a written design document and a small proof-of-concept in a separate package, not full production implementation.",
    "Code reuse from XD will be maximized by copying only minimal classes (e.g., Tuple JSON support) and rewriting the module entry points as s-c-s @Configuration classes.",
    "All new modules will target Java 17+ to comply with the Spring Framework 6.0 / Spring Cloud Stream baseline.",
    "Testing will follow the existing s-c-s test conventions: unit tests with JUnit 5/Mockito and integration tests annotated with Spring Boot test slices."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Spring XD source code is available and accessible for reference (publicly open source).",
    "The target repository is Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) and uses Maven for builds.",
    "An existing Kafka binder is already wired in; the BinderFactory work is for extensibility, not to introduce a new binder.",
    "ZooKeeper client libraries (Apache Curator) are available in the XD codebase and can be referenced for the U7 design spike.",
    "The developer performing the work has prior experience with both Spring XD and Spring Cloud Stream internals.",
    "Code review is performed by the same developer for self-review only (as per the prompt's premise that one developer does all work).",
    "No infrastructure or environment provisioning (CI setup, repository creation) is required beyond local build configuration updates.",
    "Documentation means updating module-level README files; no marketing or release-notes work is in scope.",
    "Effort figures represent active development/analysis time only and exclude meetings, breaks, or context-switching overhead beyond a small review/integration line item."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Familiarize with XD module architecture and set up s-c-s module skeleton",
      "activity_description": "Review the existing Spring XD processor module structure, study the s-c-s processor conventions, and prepare a common module skeleton (Maven module, base @Configuration, test fixtures) that all five ported modules can reuse.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Port json-to-tuple module (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD json-to-tuple module as a s-c-s processor: deserialize incoming JSON payload into a Tuple structure, expose configuration for JSON parsing options, write unit and integration tests, add module README.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Port object-to-json module (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD object-to-json module as a s-c-s processor: serialize Java objects to JSON using Jackson, handle List/Map payloads, support configurable include/exclude properties, write unit and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Port script module (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD script module as a s-c-s processor supporting Groovy scripts that transform Message payloads. Implement script reload, variable binding, exception handling, and integration with Spring's ScriptFactory. Tests + README.",
      "most_likely_effort": 22
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Port shell module (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD shell module as a s-c-s processor that executes an external shell command, pipes the payload to stdin, and returns stdout as the output message. Implement timeout, error-stream handling, and exit-code propagation. Tests + README.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Port splitter module (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Port the XD splitter module as a s-c-s processor that splits a message into multiple output messages based on a configured SpEL expression or delimiter. Handle Iterable, array, and delimited String payloads. Tests + README.",
      "most_likely_effort": 18
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Explore composed job removal options (U6)",
      "activity_description": "Static analysis of the XD codebase to identify all classes, configuration, and runtime references to composed jobs. Produce a written design document listing 2-3 removal strategies (e.g., feature flag, runtime disable, full removal), their risks, estimated effort, and a recommendation. No production code changes in this increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Explore ZK metadata persistence for composed job definitions (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Investigate the existing ZK-based metadata layout in XD, design a scheme for persisting composed job definitions (path layout, serialization format, versioning), and build a small proof-of-concept demonstrating save/load of a job definition. Deliverable: design document + working PoC in a sandbox package.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Design and implement BinderFactory abstraction (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Define a BinderFactory interface (and default implementation) in s-c-s that returns a Binder instance for a given binder type/configuration. Refactor existing binder auto-configuration sites to consult the factory. Ensure the current Kafka binder continues to work unchanged. Add unit and integration tests verifying factory behavior with multiple registered binder types.",
      "most_likely_effort": 26
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Update parent POM, build, and test fixtures",
      "activity_description": "Register the five new modules in the s-c-s parent POM, ensure consistent plugin configuration, run the full test suite locally to confirm no regressions, and update any shared test utilities to support the new processors.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Self-review, code cleanup, and final integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Self-review of all changes for style, API consistency, and JavaDoc completeness. Run a final end-to-end integration test composing the new processors in a sample streaming pipeline. Fix any defects uncovered.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 175
  }
}
```

The script module will support both Groovy and shell-like scripting by leveraging Spring's ScriptFactory abstractions, with a unified processor contract.
The shell module will execute external processes via Java's ProcessBuilder, with a Spring Boot @ConfigurationProperties class exposing command/argument options.
The splitter module will be implemented as a Spring Integration splitter wrapped as a s-c-s processor, supporting SpEL or lambda expressions.
The json-to-tuple module will reuse the existing Tuple data structure from Spring Cloud Stream core, mapping JSON objects to Tuple fields.
The object-to-json module will use Jackson's ObjectMapper with configurable type information, exposed as a s-c-s @Transformer bean.
The BinderFactory abstraction will be modeled as a Spring FactoryBean< Binder > keyed by binder type (e.g., 'kafka', 'rabbit'), with a default implementation backed by Spring Boot auto-configuration.
The composed job removal exploration (U6) will be delivered as an analysis spike only (no code removal in this increment), producing a written design document with options and trade-offs.

The ZK metadata job definition exploration (U7) will be delivered as a design spike producing a written design document and a small proof-of-concept in a separate package, not full production implementation.
Code reuse from XD will be maximized by copying only minimal classes (e.g., Tuple JSON support) and rewriting the module entry points as s-c-s @Configuration classes.
All new modules will target Java 17+ to comply with the Spring Framework 6.0 / Spring Cloud Stream baseline.
Testing will follow the existing s-c-s test conventions: unit tests with JUnit 5/Mockito and integration tests annotated with Spring Boot test slices.
assumptions: Spring XD source code is available and accessible for reference (publicly open source).
The target repository is Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) and uses Maven for builds.
An existing Kafka binder is already wired in; the BinderFactory work is for extensibility, not to introduce a new binder.
ZooKeeper client libraries (Apache Curator) are available in the XD codebase and can be referenced for the U7 design spike.
The developer performing the work has prior experience with both Spring XD and Spring Cloud Stream internals.
Code review is performed by the same developer for self-review only (as per the prompt's premise that one developer does all work).
No infrastructure or environment provisioning (CI setup, repository creation) is required beyond local build configuration updates.
Documentation means updating module-level README files; no marketing or release-notes work is in scope.
Effort figures represent active development/analysis time only and exclude meetings, breaks, or context-switching overhead beyond a small review/integration line item.

activities.activity_name: Familiarize with XD module architecture and set up s-c-s module skeleton
activities.activity_description: Review the existing Spring XD processor module structure, study the s-c-s processor conventions, and prepare a common module skeleton (Maven module, base @Configuration, test fixtures) that all five ported modules can reuse.

Port the XD json-to-tuple module as a s-c-s processor: deserialize incoming JSON payload into a Tuple structure, expose configuration for JSON parsing options, write unit and integration tests, add module README.

Port the XD object-to-json module as a s-c-s processor: serialize Java objects to JSON using Jackson, handle List/Map payloads, support configurable include/exclude properties, write unit and integration tests.

Port the XD script module as a s-c-s processor supporting Groovy scripts that transform Message payloads. Implement script reload, variable binding, exception handling, and integration with Spring's ScriptFactory. Tests + README.

Port the XD shell module as a s-c-s processor that executes an external shell command, pipes the payload to stdin, and returns stdout as the output message. Implement timeout, error-stream handling, and exit-code propagation. Tests + README.

Port the XD splitter module as a s-c-s processor that splits a message into multiple output messages based on a configured SpEL expression or delimiter. Handle Iterable, array, and delimited String payloads. Tests + README.

Static analysis of the XD codebase to identify all classes, configuration, and runtime references to composed jobs. Produce a written design document listing 2-3 removal strategies (e.g., feature flag, runtime disable, full removal), their risks, estimated effort, and a recommendation. No production code changes in this increment.
